elaras_silver_ring.name: plain silver ring
elaras_silver_ring.lore: This small ring of tarnished silver was worn smooth by a child's restless fingers. It has no enchantment and no hidden power, but only the fierce love of a little girl who believed it to be the most precious thing in the world, and it may be that in a way she was right.

ring_of_invisibility.name: ring of invisibility
ring_of_invisibility.lore: For the war against the Titans the Cyclopes made three gifts, the thunderbolt for Zeus and the trident for Poseidon, and for Hades a cap that hid its wearer from every eye. Perseus borrowed that cap to escape the sisters of Medusa, and a sliver of the same craft is set in the clear stone of this ring, to hide whoever wears it.

ring_curse_teleport.name: ring of teleportitis
ring_curse_teleport.lore: Hera sent a gadfly to torment Io, and by its sting she was driven without rest across the known world, so that the strait she swam is named after her still, the Bosporus or Ox-Ford. A sting of the same sort is held in the cracked stone of this ring, and whoever wears it is forever being sent away to some other place.

ring_curse_aggravate.name: ring of aggravation
ring_curse_aggravate.lore: The hunter Actaeon beheld Artemis at her bathing, and the goddess changed him into a stag. His own fifty hounds caught the scent and ran him down, never knowing their master. Some part of that scent clings to this gaudy ring, so that every beast within earshot wakes hungry and turns toward the one who wears it.

ring_curse_fumble.name: ring of fumbling
ring_curse_fumble.lore: In some forgotten port a thieves' guild punished one of its members for stealing from his fellows by locking a ring of lead upon his hand. Never again could he hold lockpick, purse or knife for longer than a breath. The guild is long gone, but the ring has gone on seeking other hands that it may punish.

ring_curse_slow.name: ring of slowing
ring_curse_slow.lore: Swift Achilles could never overtake a tortoise that had the start of him, argued Zeno of Elea, for each time he reached the place where it had been, it had crawled a little farther. The philosophers named this a paradox, but whoever wears this band of black iron must live within it, and be always one step behind.

amulet_curse_teleport.name: amulet of teleportitis
amulet_curse_teleport.lore: As the prophet Habakkuk bore a bowl of stew to the reapers, an angel caught him by the hair and set him down in Babylon over the lions' den to feed Daniel, and afterward carried him home. This split pendant has kept the journey but has lost both angel and purpose, and it snatches its wearer away for no reason at all.

amulet_curse_slow.name: amulet of slowing
amulet_curse_slow.lore: It would be better for a man, the Gospel says, to have a millstone hung about his neck and be cast into the sea than to lead a child astray. A magistrate who was fond of scripture had these grey medals made for his prisoners, and though they weigh almost nothing in the hand, upon the neck they drag as heavily as that millstone.

dragonslayer_ring.name: Dragonslayer's Ring
dragonslayer_ring.lore: Old King Beowulf, when the dragon woke, had a shield made all of iron, for he knew that linden wood would burn. Eleven chosen men went with him to the barrow, and ten fled to the trees, so that Wiglaf alone stood in the fire beside his lord. Out of that hoard came this scorched ring of gold, and it remembers who it was that stood fast against the dragon and the flame.

shadow_walker_ring.name: Shadow Walker's Ring
shadow_walker_ring.lore: The master of an ancient guild of thieves, whose trade was in assassinations too perilous for common hands, wore this ring of lustreless black that seems to drink the light about it. Its gold and its venom-glands were stripped from one and the same dead king, and the band smells faintly of nightshade still. The blood of whoever wears it will cease to take any notice of poison.

philosophers_ring.name: Philosopher's Ring
philosophers_ring.lore: Upon the hand that held his quill the first philosopher of this dungeon wore this ring, and graven on it in little is the ouroboros of the Philosopher's Shard. Since all his searching after knowledge passed of old through those fingers, the metal still grows warm to the touch when unknown things are near.

ring_of_sustenance.name: ring of sustenance
ring_of_sustenance.lore: A widow of Zarephath had but a handful of meal and a little oil left when the prophet Elijah lodged with her in the great drought, and she fed him first. Thereafter the jar of meal and the cruse of oil did not run out until the rains came, and they say that a drop of that oil hardened into the amber of this ring.

amulet_life_saving.name: amulet of life saving
amulet_life_saving.lore: When death was appointed for King Admetus, his wife Alcestis consented to die in his stead, and she was borne to the tomb. But Heracles was a guest in that house of mourning, and he went out by night and lay in wait for Death beside her grave, and wrestled with him until he was forced to yield her up. The strength of that grip endures in this warm medal of gold, and it will deliver the one who wears it from death a single time.

ring_of_spell_turning.name: ring of spell turning
ring_of_spell_turning.lore: King Balak of Moab hired the seer Balaam to curse Israel and brought him up three mountains for that purpose, yet three times Balaam opened his mouth and uttered a blessing, while the curse fell back upon the man who had paid for it. By the spiral cut in this ring ill words are turned aside in the same manner, so that the blows of magic, of shadow and of the mind glance off.

ring_curse_drain.name: ring of life drain
ring_curse_drain.lore: For felling an oak that was sacred to Demeter, Erysichthon had Hunger sent by the goddess to breathe upon him as he slept. He ate up his herds and sold all that he owned for food, and at the last, as Ovid tells, he gnawed his own limbs. This cold ring has the same appetite, and of all that it might feed upon, its wearer lies nearest.

amulet_curse_drain.name: amulet of doom
amulet_curse_drain.unidentified_name: a sword-shaped pendant on a hair-thin chain
amulet_curse_drain.lore: Damocles praised the good fortune of kings to Dionysius, the tyrant of Syracuse, who seated him upon the throne at a banquet with a sword hung above his head by a single horsehair, and he had no more appetite for the feast. Whoever wears this pendant sits beneath that sword in his place, and the hair is fraying.

ring_of_gyges.name: Ring of Gyges
ring_of_gyges.unidentified_name: a plain band that seems to blur at the edges
ring_of_gyges.lore: An earthquake once opened the ground before Gyges, a Lydian shepherd, as Glaucon tells in Plato's Republic, and within a hollow horse of bronze he found a dead man who wore a ring of gold. When he turned the bezel inward he became invisible, and by that power he won over the queen, killed the king and took the throne. Then Glaucon asked whether anyone who had such a ring would remain just.

ring_of_the_nibelung.name: Ring of the Nibelung
ring_of_the_nibelung.unidentified_name: a heavy gold ring with a tiny rune
ring_of_the_nibelung.lore: Andvari the dwarf swore that this ring should be the death of all who owned it, when Loki took it from him to pay the blood-price for Otr. For its sake Fafnir killed his father Hreidmar, and Sigurd killed Fafnir and was himself murdered in his bed. Gunnar and Hogni sank the hoard in the Rhine, and they died in the hall of Atli without ever telling where it lay.

andvaranaut.name: Andvaranaut
andvaranaut.unidentified_name: a golden ring that seems lighter than it should
andvaranaut.lore: Beneath a waterfall the dwarf Andvari lived in the shape of a pike and guarded his gold, until Loki borrowed the net of the sea-goddess Ran, hauled him out and took all that he had. The dwarf begged to keep one small ring, for with it he could make his wealth grow again, but Loki took that also. Its name means Andvari's Gift, and it was a bitter jest of the dwarf's to call it so, when he had never willingly given it.

draupnir.name: Draupnir
draupnir.unidentified_name: a golden ring of incredible craftsmanship
draupnir.lore: Brokkr and Sindri, brothers of the dwarf race, forged Draupnir at the same smithing as Mjölnir, and eight new gold rings of equal weight drip from it every ninth night. Odin laid it on the pyre of Baldr, and Baldr sent it back from Hel in proof that he still had being. Even now gold finds its way to the hand that wears it.

ring_of_eluned.name: Ring of Eluned
ring_of_eluned.unidentified_name: a green ring of twisted ivy-metal
ring_of_eluned.lore: Owain pursued a wounded knight through a castle gate, as the Welsh tale of the Lady of the Fountain relates, and the portcullis fell behind him, cutting his horse in two, and left him trapped between the gates. Then the maiden Luned passed him a ring through the bars and told him that if he turned the stone inward and closed his hand over it no one would see him, and so it proved in the hour of his need.

brisingamen.name: Brisingamen
brisingamen.unidentified_name: a necklace of four interlocked golden torcs
brisingamen.lore: Alfrigg, Dvalin, Berling and Grer were the four dwarves who made the necklace of Freyja. Loki crept into her bower as a fly to steal it, and Heimdall fought him for it upon a skerry with both of them in the shape of seals, and once Thor wore it beneath a bridal veil to win back his hammer. Whenever Freyja weeps for Od, her lost husband, the tears that she sheds are of red gold.

talisman_of_troy.name: Palladium of Troy
talisman_of_troy.unidentified_name: a small wooden figure of armed Athena
talisman_of_troy.lore: Out of the sky there fell into Troy a wooden image of armed Athena, which was called the Palladium, and while it stayed within the walls the city could not be taken. Odysseus and Diomedes therefore crept in by night and bore it away. In after years Rome claimed that Aeneas had saved the true one, and kept it in the temple of Vesta, where none but the Vestals might look upon it.

eye_of_horus.name: Eye of Horus
eye_of_horus.lore: Horus had his eye torn out by Set when they strove for the throne of Egypt, but Thoth found the pieces and made it whole, and Horus gave it to Osiris his dead father to restore him. The Egyptians called it the wedjat, which is the sound eye, and painted it on coffins and upon the prows of boats. Slowly, and with no great show, it mends whatever hurts its wearer has taken.

scarab_of_khepri.name: Scarab of Khepri
scarab_of_khepri.unidentified_name: a jade ring shaped like a beetle
scarab_of_khepri.lore: The scarab rolls its ball of dung across the sand and buries it, and the Egyptians, who saw young beetles afterward climb out of the ground as if from nothing, gave that beetle's face to Khepri, the god who pushes the sun above the horizon each morning. In the same fashion the beetle carved upon this ring renews whoever wears it, by a little with every dawn.

hamsa_hand.name: Hand of Fatima
hamsa_hand.unidentified_name: an open hand amulet with an eye in the palm
hamsa_hand.lore: Older than any of the faiths that wear it now is the open hand with an eye in its palm. The Muslims name it the Hand of Fatima, the Jews the Hand of Miriam, and some Christians of the East the Hand of Mary, and its other name, Khamsa, is simply the Arabic word for five. In every house it has the same office, which is to turn the envious glance back upon the one who cast it.

ouroboros_pendant.name: Ouroboros
ouroboros_pendant.unidentified_name: a silver pendant of a serpent eating its tail
ouroboros_pendant.lore: Upon a gilded shrine in the tomb of Tutankhamun appears the first serpent that swallows its own tail, circling the head and feet of a god. Afterward Greek alchemists in Egypt took up the sign, and the one called Cleopatra drew it about three words, 'the all is one.' What the serpent eats of itself it grows again, and so will the flesh of whoever wears its likeness.

necklace_of_harmonia.name: Necklace of Harmonia
necklace_of_harmonia.unidentified_name: a golden necklace of impossible craftsmanship
necklace_of_harmonia.lore: Hephaestus bore a grudge against the mother of Harmonia, and when Harmonia became the bride of Cadmus of Thebes he made her this necklace for a wedding gift, to the ruin of all who owned it. With it Polynices bribed Eriphyle, who sent her husband to die in the war of the Seven against Thebes, and for that deed her own son killed her. At the last it was hung up in Delphi, where no one could wear it.

menat_of_hathor.name: Menat of Hathor
menat_of_hathor.unidentified_name: a beaded collar of carnelian and faience
menat_of_hathor.lore: The menat was the sacred necklace of Hathor, which was shaken as a rattle in her rites, being at once jewellery and an instrument of music. The reliefs of her temples show pharaohs receiving it from the goddess as a pledge of health, fertility and joy, and her priests held that in the sound of its carnelian beads, as they struck one upon another, was the sound of all things being well.

heart_of_ahriman.name: Heart of Ahriman
heart_of_ahriman.unidentified_name: a deep red gem that seems to pulse
heart_of_ahriman.lore: For every good thing that Ohrmazd made, the Zoroastrians teach, the Hostile Spirit Ahriman made something to spoil it: winter against summer, the lie against the truth, and against the healthy body ninety-nine thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine diseases. This red stone has knowledge of how each made thing comes apart, and it is warm in the hand as no stone ought to be.

tyet_of_isis.name: Tyet of Isis
tyet_of_isis.unidentified_name: a knotted red jasper amulet like a tied sash
tyet_of_isis.lore: At the throat of the dead the embalmers of Egypt laid the tyet, cut from red jasper, which looks like an ankh with folded arms or like the knot in a sash. The Book of the Dead gives the spell to be spoken over it, calling upon the blood and the power of Isis, for she had brought her own husband back from death and might do as much again.

idunn_apple_charm.name: Idunn's Apple
idunn_apple_charm.unidentified_name: a carved jade apple on a silver chain
idunn_apple_charm.lore: It was Idunn who kept the golden apples that gave the Aesir eternal youth, and when Loki suffered the giant Thjazi to steal her away, the gods began to grow old. They compelled him to fetch her back, and in the shape of a falcon he turned her into a nut and flew homeward with her. Thjazi pursued them until the gods lit fires at the walls of Asgard and the giant was burned. So great was the worth of Idunn that by her absence alone she had brought all the gods into peril.

caduceus_charm.name: Caduceus Amulet
caduceus_charm.unidentified_name: a charm of two serpents coiled around a winged rod
caduceus_charm.lore: In return for the lyre that Hermes had invented, Apollo gave him a staff of gold, and with it the god closes the eyes of those who wake, opens the eyes of sleepers, and leads the dead down the road to Hades. The story goes that he once thrust it between two snakes as they fought, and that they have twined about it in peace ever since.

torque_of_lugh.name: Torque of Lugh
torque_of_lugh.unidentified_name: a twisted gold neck-ring of Celtic make
torque_of_lugh.lore: Lugh came to Tara and was turned away by the doorkeeper, who said that the Tuatha De Danann had already a smith and a champion, a harper, a poet and a physician. But when Lugh asked whether they had one man who was all of these at once they had none, and the king gave him the seat of the sage. Irish heroes were wont to wear gold at the throat, and this torque was his own.

pectoral_of_amun.name: Pectoral of Amun
pectoral_of_amun.unidentified_name: a broad chest ornament of lapis and gold
pectoral_of_amun.lore: The name of Amun signifies the Hidden One, and his image dwelt in the darkness at the back of the temple of Karnak, and was veiled even when the priests bore it forth on its gilded boat. Pharaohs brought their questions to it, and upon the shoulders of the bearers the boat would dip forward for yes or draw back for no.

ankh_of_ra.name: Ankh of Ra
ankh_of_ra.unidentified_name: a looped cross of gilded bronze
ankh_of_ra.lore: Upon temple walls the gods hold the ankh by its loop as one holds a key, and press it to the lips of a king to give him breath. None knows for certain what the sign first pictured, though it may well have been the strap of a sandal, and the Christians of Egypt kept it as a cross with a handle. This one is of bronze, gilded with the color of the sun god.

ring_of_gawain.name: Ring of Sir Gawain
ring_of_gawain.unidentified_name: a plain green ring with a small enameled star
ring_of_gawain.lore: Each morning from nine until noon the strength of Gawain increased, as Sir Thomas Malory tells, until he fought with the might of three men, and afterward it ebbed away. The older poem gives him a pentangle upon his shield and, after his one small lie to the Green Knight, a green sash that he wore as a badge of shame. But the whole court put on the sash to do him honor.

ring_of_odysseus.name: Ring of Odysseus
ring_of_odysseus.unidentified_name: an old bronze ring with a ship carved in the stone
ring_of_odysseus.lore: A ship is graven on the stone of this ring, for Odysseus was ten years upon the road home from Troy, and he came through because he took note of all things. He noted the trick of the Cyclops's doorstone, the wax that would stop the ears of his crew against the Sirens, and the test that Penelope set him with the bed which he had built himself about a living olive tree. From such a ring nothing that is hidden can stay hidden for long.

ring_of_scheherazade.name: Ring of Scheherazade
ring_of_scheherazade.unidentified_name: a ring set with a pale blue stone that swirls
ring_of_scheherazade.lore: King Shahryar took a new bride every evening and had her put to death at dawn, until Scheherazade, the daughter of the vizier, offered herself. On the wedding night her sister Dunyazad begged a story of her, and she broke it off at daybreak just short of the ending, so that the king let her live one day more to hear it. In this fashion she saved her life through a thousand and one nights.

amulet_of_merlin.name: Amulet of Merlin
amulet_of_merlin.unidentified_name: a blue pendant with a moving star inside the stone
amulet_of_merlin.lore: Merlin was born of an incubus and a Welsh princess, yet the people of his day were little troubled by it. He counselled three kings, raised Stonehenge as some accounts have it, created the Round Table and contrived the begetting of Arthur. In the end his pupil Nimue imprisoned him, and there he remained, though some tellers make his prison a tower of glass and others a tree or a cave.

ring_of_pythia.name: Ring of the Oracle
ring_of_pythia.unidentified_name: a bronze ring smelling faintly of laurel smoke
ring_of_pythia.lore: Over a chasm in the earth at Delphi sat the Pythia, breathing its volcanic vapour, and spoke for Apollo in words that were famous for their double meaning. Croesus was told that if he attacked Persia he would destroy a great empire, and so he did, but the empire was his own. The Oracle was never wrong, and it needed only that those who heard should read its words with care.

anklet_of_atalanta.name: Anklet of Atalanta
anklet_of_atalanta.unidentified_name: a delicate runner's anklet of pale silver
anklet_of_atalanta.lore: No man alive could outrun Atalanta, and her father offered her hand to whoever could beat her in a race, while those who lost were killed. Hippomenes won by letting fall three golden apples of Aphrodite, which she stopped to gather up. She cared little for the apples, but to lose seemed to her more interesting than anything that had yet befallen her.

crown_of_croesus.name: Diadem of Croesus
crown_of_croesus.unidentified_name: a ring cut from a broken golden diadem
crown_of_croesus.lore: Croesus of Lydia was the richest man in the world and knew it well. Before he would ask the Delphic Oracle whether he should attack Persia, he made trial of its power with an absurd question, and it answered truly. It answered truly of Persia also, but he misread what it had said and attacked to his own undoing, so that the fault was his and none of the Oracle's.

collar_of_njord.name: Sea-Collar of Njörd
collar_of_njord.unidentified_name: a necklace of Baltic amber and whale-bone
collar_of_njord.lore: Njord has the rule of the wind and the sea and the luck of fishermen. The giantess Skadi was permitted to choose a husband from among the gods by looking at their feet alone, and she picked the handsomest pair, hoping for Baldr, and found that she had the god of the sea. But he could not sleep in her mountains for the howling of wolves, and she could not sleep at his harbor for the screaming of the gulls.

ring_of_percival.name: Ring of the Pure Knight
ring_of_percival.unidentified_name: a silver ring set with a small cup-shaped hollow
ring_of_percival.lore: A kind old knight had taught young Percival that it is discourteous to talk too much, and so when he saw the Grail carried through the hall of the wounded Fisher King he said nothing, though one question would have healed the king and his wasted land. He spent long years in finding that castle again that he might ask it, and the small hollow in this ring has the shape of the cup that he sought.

ring_of_lancelot.name: Ring of the Fallen Knight
ring_of_lancelot.unidentified_name: a red-gold ring with a small tower engraved on it
ring_of_lancelot.lore: Lancelot was fostered by the Lady of the Lake, who did not tell him his name. He learned it when he had won the castle of Dolorous Gard and raised a slab in its graveyard, for his own name was cut beneath as that of the man who would one day lie there. He called the place Joyous Gard thereafter, and it is that castle whose tower is on this ring, and there he lies buried.

seal_of_agrippa.name: Seal of Agrippa
seal_of_agrippa.unidentified_name: a wax seal pendant with planetary symbols
seal_of_agrippa.lore: Three Books of Occult Philosophy were published in 1531 by Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa, who gathered into them all the magic of the Renaissance under one order of three worlds, the elemental, the celestial and the intellectual. He was accused of heresy and employed by kings and died in debt, and no books of magic were so widely read in the 16th century as his. Toward the end he himself declared them worthless, though it is likely that in this he was not altogether honest.

philosophers_ring_legendary.name: Philosopher's Ring of Mastery
philosophers_ring_legendary.unidentified_name: a ring of strange alloy that seems to look back at you
philosophers_ring_legendary.lore: From his childhood Socrates had heard a voice that never told him what to do, but only stopped him when he was about to do wrong, and he trusted it above every argument. An old catalogue lists this ring among the goods of Plato's Academy, but the entry breaks off in the middle of a sentence, and no more can be learned of it, for the last page is missing.
philosophers_ring_legendary.special: A voice stops you when you are about to answer wrong: three times a floor, a wrong choice is struck out and you choose again.

amulet_of_pythagoras.name: Tetractys Amulet
amulet_of_pythagoras.unidentified_name: a bronze triangle pendant with ten points
amulet_of_pythagoras.lore: The Pythagoreans of Croton swore their oaths by the tetractys, a triangle of ten points in rows of one, two, three and four, which holds the ratios of the musical scale. It was a rule among them besides that they should eat no beans. One of them, Hippasus, is said to have shown that the diagonal of a square cannot be measured by its side, and to have been drowned at sea for letting it be known.

ring_of_hypatia.name: Ring of Hypatia
ring_of_hypatia.unidentified_name: a thin bronze ring engraved with mathematical diagrams
ring_of_hypatia.lore: Foremost among the mathematicians and astronomers of her age was Hypatia of Alexandria, head of the Neoplatonic school and counsellor to the prefect Orestes. Her father Theon had reared her to be 'a perfect human being.' In 415 CE a Christian mob pulled her from her chariot, dragged her to a church and killed her, and it was through no imperfection of hers that she perished, but because those about her could not endure the example that she set.

ring_of_thunder.name: Ring of Thunder
ring_of_thunder.unidentified_name: a ring set with a chip of grey stone
ring_of_thunder.lore: Farmers in every country of Europe who turned up an axe of polished stone in the furrow would take it for a thunderbolt grown cold, and they kept such thunderstones beneath the eaves, reasoning that lightning does not strike twice in one place. A chip of one is set in this ring, and as it wards off the lightning, so also it sharpens the wits.

amulet_of_the_titan.name: Amulet of the Titan
amulet_of_the_titan.unidentified_name: a lump of dark ore on a chain
amulet_of_the_titan.lore: When ten years of war were ended Zeus shut the Titans in Tartarus, so deep that a bronze anvil let fall from heaven, as Hesiod reckons it, would be nine days and nights in reaching the earth, and nine more from the earth to that prison. This lump of dark ore is said to come from the bottom of it, and though it is heavier than it looks, it makes the wearer equal to the weight.

ring_of_the_deep.name: Ring of the Deep
ring_of_the_deep.lore: Herodotus tells of Scyllias of Scione, the best diver of his age, who salvaged treasure for the Persians from their wrecked ships and afterward deserted to the Greeks. People said that he swam the whole way beneath the water, some ten miles, though Herodotus himself thought it likelier that he took a boat. The ring that Scyllias wore still glows faintly blue, and whoever wears it does not feel the cold.

amulet_of_insight.name: Amulet of Insight
amulet_of_insight.unidentified_name: a clear crystal on a laurel-wood disc
amulet_of_insight.lore: At the entrance of Apollo's temple at Delphi every pilgrim passed by two sayings that were carved there, 'Know thyself' and 'Nothing in excess.' For such as could not remember two things at once the priests sold little copies, and this is one of them. The mind of one who wears it is not so easily frightened, flattered or confused.

ring_of_the_assassin.name: Ring of the Assassin
ring_of_the_assassin.unidentified_name: a black signet with a dagger device
ring_of_the_assassin.lore: Without a siege Hasan-i Sabbah took the mountain castle of Alamut, the Eagle's Nest, in 1090, and out of it he sent men singly with daggers against viziers and princes. It held for a hundred and sixty-six years, until the Mongols under Hulegu threw it down. This black signet left by a side gate, and whoever wears it walks very quietly, as those men were wont to do.

amulet_of_fortitude.name: Amulet of Fortitude
amulet_of_fortitude.unidentified_name: a bronze amulet with a coiled serpent
amulet_of_fortitude.lore: The sick would come to the temples of Asclepius that they might sleep there. In the long porch at Epidaurus they lay down, while the harmless serpents of the god moved among them in the dark, and in the morning they told the priests their dreams and were treated. One of those serpents is coiled in bronze upon this amulet, and beneath it flesh mends and fevers break.

ring_of_far_sight.name: Ring of Far Sight
ring_of_far_sight.unidentified_name: a ring set with an eye-like green gem
ring_of_far_sight.lore: Lynceus was the lookout of the Argo, and the poets say that his eyes were so keen that he could see through the trunk of an oak and tell what lay buried under the ground. Once from a mountaintop he espied two men who were hidden inside a hollow tree. The green stone that is set in this ring narrows and widens like the pupil of such an eye.

amulet_of_the_archmage.name: Amulet of the Archmage
amulet_of_the_archmage.unidentified_name: a blackened bronze amulet, warm to the touch
amulet_of_the_archmage.lore: Empedocles of Sicily taught that all things are made of four roots, which are fire, air, water and earth. Legend says that at the last he leaped into the crater of Etna to prove himself a god, and that the volcano threw back one of his bronze sandals, of which this amulet was cast. Fire has had its turn with that metal already, and so it does less harm to whoever bears the amulet.

ring_of_displacement.name: Ring of Displacement
ring_of_displacement.unidentified_name: a ring set with a wavering grey gem
ring_of_displacement.lore: Castles and harbors are sometimes seen standing in the air above the Strait of Messina, where there is nothing at all, and the sailors name that sight Fata Morgana, after Morgan le Fay, and steer well clear of it. Some of that air is held in the grey gem of this ring, so that its wearer is quick upon his feet and is never quite where he appears to be.

amulet_of_protection.name: Amulet of Protection
amulet_of_protection.unidentified_name: a red clay amulet stamped with a dragon
amulet_of_protection.lore: Marduk of Babylon went out to battle with Tiamat, the dragon of the salt sea, bearing a charm of red paste between his lips and a herb against poison in his hand, as the old poem tells. The priests of his house at Esagila pressed copies in red clay for travellers, and upon this one spells are broken as waves are broken upon a mole.

sphinx_crown.name: Sphinx's Crown
sphinx_crown.lore: The Sphinx sat upon a rock outside Thebes and asked every traveller what goes on four legs in the morning, two at noon and three in the evening, and she ate those who failed. When Oedipus answered 'Man,' she threw herself from the rock, but her crown remained behind, and it steadies the mind of anyone who must give an answer under pressure.

sailors_amulet.name: Sailor's Amulet
sailors_amulet.lore: Three times a day Charybdis swallows the sea, and three times she spews it forth. After Zeus had wrecked his last ship Odysseus drifted back over her, and he hung like a bat from the fig tree above the whirlpool until she gave back his mast and keel. This amulet was whittled from that timber, and its wearer feels trouble coming as a sailor feels the weather, and does not mind the cold.

anubis_scales.name: Anubis's Scales
anubis_scales.lore: Jackal-headed Anubis, in the Hall of Two Truths, sets the dead man's heart in one pan of the scale and the feather of Ma'at in the other, and Thoth writes down the outcome. Beside them waits Ammit, who is part crocodile, part lion and part hippopotamus, for the hearts that fail. This is a small likeness of those scales, and it keeps steady the heart of one who yet lives.

ring_of_iron_grip.name: Ring of Iron Grip
ring_of_iron_grip.lore: Ravana, the ten-headed king of Lanka, once strove to tear Mount Kailash out of the ground and bear it away, but Shiva pressed down with one toe and pinned him beneath it, and for a thousand years he sang hymns before he was released. Out of a link of the demon king's armor this crude band of iron was beaten, and like the mountain's hold upon him, its grip does not loosen.

obsidian_talisman.name: Obsidian Talisman
obsidian_talisman.lore: Hunahpu and Xbalanque, the Hero Twins of the Maya, were tested by the lords of Xibalba, the underworld, in a row of houses, as the Popol Vuh tells: the Dark House, the Cold House, the Jaguar House, the Bat House, and the Razor House that was full of living blades of obsidian. They came through them all, and this shard is from the last, so that darkness does not hide much from the eyes of its bearer.

ariadnes_thread.name: Ariadne's Thread
ariadnes_thread.unidentified_name: a ball of silver thread on a belt-hook
ariadnes_thread.lore: Before Theseus went in to face the Minotaur, Ariadne the daughter of King Minos gave him a ball of thread. He tied one end to the door of the Labyrinth and let it run out behind him, and it led him back again, yet on the voyage home he left her upon the isle of Naxos. The thread has forgotten not a single turning of that road.

eponas_charm.name: Epona's Charm
eponas_charm.lore: Among the Gauls Epona was the goddess of horses, and she is shown riding side-saddle with a foal at her knee. Horsemen of Gaul who served in the cavalry of Rome bore her east and south until her shrine stood in every stable of the empire, and of all Celtic gods she alone was honored in Rome itself. Her charm keeps the traveller off the bad road and out of the blind alley.

anansis_thread.name: Anansi's Thread
anansis_thread.unidentified_name: a cord braided from spider silk
anansis_thread.lore: All the stories in the world belonged to the sky god Nyame, and when Anansi the spider asked for them he named a price that none could pay: Onini the python, Osebo the leopard and the Mmoboro hornets, delivered alive. Anansi tricked each of them into a trap of its own choosing, and the Akan have called every tale a spider story since that day. Whatever is learned by one who wears this cord will stay learned.

rope_of_izanagi.name: Rope of Izanagi
rope_of_izanagi.unidentified_name: a shimenawa rope that hums with spiritual energy
rope_of_izanagi.lore: To bring his wife Izanami home from Yomi, the land of the dead, Izanagi went down into it, but he fled when he saw what she had become. At the pass out of the underworld he rolled across the road a boulder that a thousand men could not move. Such a boundary is marked in Japan by a rope of twisted straw, and this rope hums when anything hidden is near.

silverlight_pendant.name: Silverlight Pendant
silverlight_pendant.lore: This small pendant of silver hangs upon a fine chain, and it is warm to the touch, as if someone had held it only a little while ago. The name 'ELARA' is graven on the back in a child's unsteady hand.

saints_reliquary.name: Saint's Reliquary
saints_reliquary.unidentified_name: a silver reliquary containing a saint's fingerbone
saints_reliquary.lore: A monk bore this silver case, no longer than a thumb, down into the deep places, and he crawled the last corridors on hands and knees lest he should fall with it, for behind its window of rock crystal lies the fingerbone of a saint. It is faintly warm, and both mind and body rest more easily when it is near.

officers_signet.name: Officer's Signet
officers_signet.unidentified_name: a heavy gold signet ring stamped with the Legion crest
officers_signet.lore: Signets such as this, of solid gold and bearing the crest of the Legion, were given only to those who had earned a command. The last to hold it gave it up of his own will, saying that he did not deserve it, and the ring itself passes judgement on no one. It makes the hand that wears it stronger and surer, and it leaves to the wearer the question of who is deserving.

prophets_amulet.name: Prophet's Amulet
prophets_amulet.unidentified_name: an amulet pulsing with gathered visions
prophets_amulet.lore: An old prophet wore this amulet through the last years of his life, while he cut warnings into tablets of stone for those who should come after, of the Destroyer, the Seven Seals and the final battle. Something of what he beheld has soaked into it, so that the clearness it gives to the mind is very near to pain.

aesops_quill.name: Aesop's Quill
aesops_quill.lore: Aesop was a slave upon the island of Samos, as Herodotus says, and tradition adds that he talked his way to freedom with his tales, of the tortoise who beat the hare, the boy who cried wolf and the fox who decided that the grapes were sour in any case. This ring in the shape of a feather belonged to a freedman, and it helps its wearer to see the plain point of a thing.

lyre_of_orpheus.name: Lyre of Orpheus
lyre_of_orpheus.unidentified_name: an amulet shaped like a tiny lyre
lyre_of_orpheus.lore: So sweetly did Orpheus play that trees pulled up their roots to follow him and rivers stayed their course to listen. For his wife Eurydice he went down to Hades, where he sang the three-headed hound to sleep and moved Persephone to tears, and only by looking back did he lose her. This tiny lyre hums still, and no spell of sleep can close the eyes of anyone who hears it.

tablet_of_gilgamesh.name: Tablet of Gilgamesh
tablet_of_gilgamesh.unidentified_name: a clay ring inscribed with cuneiform
tablet_of_gilgamesh.lore: After he had watched his friend Enkidu die, Gilgamesh, king of Uruk, journeyed to the end of the world to learn how he might escape death. At the bottom of the sea he found the plant that restores youth, but a snake ate it while he bathed, and he went home and looked upon the walls that he had built. Stamped in the clay of this ring is a line of his story, which is the oldest story there is.

scales_of_maat.name: Scales of Ma'at
scales_of_maat.unidentified_name: a ring with tiny golden scales
scales_of_maat.lore: Ma'at is truth itself, and her sign is a single feather of the ostrich, against which the heart of every dead Egyptian was weighed in the Hall of Two Truths. If it was no heavier than the feather it passed on to the Field of Reeds, and if it was heavy it went to Ammit the Devourer. The tiny scales upon this ring help the one who wears it to weigh things as they truly are.

tablet_of_hammurabi.name: Tablet of Hammurabi
tablet_of_hammurabi.unidentified_name: a heavy clay amulet covered in ancient script
tablet_of_hammurabi.lore: Hammurabi of Babylon, about 1750 BC, caused 282 laws to be cut on a pillar of black stone taller than a man and set where anyone might read them, and at its head the sun god Shamash hands him the rod and ring of kingship. 'An eye for an eye' is among those laws, and this amulet of clay is copied from one corner of the pillar.

torc_of_boudicca.name: Torc of Boudicca
torc_of_boudicca.lore: Boudicca, queen of the Iceni, was a tall woman, with a great mass of tawny hair to her hips and a heavy torc of gold at her throat. When the Romans flogged her and wronged her daughters in AD 60, she burned Camulodunum, Londinium and Verulamium to the ground. Her torc lends her temper to the one who wears it, so that the body will not break nor the mind bend, however many foes crowd in.

rands_heart.name: Rand's Heart
rands_heart.lore: A simple silver locket on a leather thong. It is infused with the power of a lover's promise. He knew he could not always be by Robyn's side, but he swore to protect her, always.

dreamspun_sketchbook.name: Dreamspun Sketchbook
dreamspun_sketchbook.lore: A young lady's sketchbook. It's full of whimsical drawings. She used this sketchbook to bring her dreams to life. The pages shimmer with magical energy.

charmander_stuffie.name: Charmander Stuffie
charmander_stuffie.lore: A child's favorite toy and oldest friend. It looks like a small orange dragon with a burning ember on the tip of its tail. The love shown to this toy has imbued it with a shimmering magical power that protects and strengthens the bearer.

jade_cicada.name: Jade Cicada
jade_cicada.lore: After years beneath the ground the cicada climbs into the light, splits its old skin and flies away, and so mourners in Han China laid a cicada of carved jade upon the tongue of the dead, hoping that the body might do likewise. This one was never buried, and when a blow should kill its wearer the jade will crack instead, and yet will hold, so that life is not lost.

seal_of_solomon.name: Seal of Solomon
seal_of_solomon.unidentified_name: a bronze ring engraved with a six-pointed star
seal_of_solomon.lore: While a boy was labouring upon the Temple, as the Testament of Solomon relates, a demon tormented him, and when Solomon prayed the Archangel Michael brought him a ring with a seal cut in its stone. The boy threw it at the demon's chest and led him back bound, and with that ring Solomon set the demons to hauling stone. Lesser beings will still halt where they stand when its wearer speaks.

ankh_of_isis.name: Ankh of Isis
ankh_of_isis.unidentified_name: a golden cross with a looped top
ankh_of_isis.lore: When Set had cut the body of Osiris into fourteen pieces and scattered them along the Nile, Isis searched the whole river in a boat of papyrus. What she found she gathered and bound together, and with her wings she fanned breath back into her husband. This ankh was hers, and what she did for him it will do once for its wearer, though it will not itself survive the effort.

megingjord.name: Megingjörð
megingjord.lore: Thor had three treasures, as Snorri numbers them: the hammer Mjolnir, the iron gloves without which he cannot grip it, and the belt Megingjord, which doubles his divine strength when he buckles it on. Such was the strength that he used on the day when he hooked the World-Serpent with the head of an ox for bait, and braced himself so hard that both his feet went through the bottom of the boat.

kavacha_kundala.name: Kavacha and Kundala
kavacha_kundala.lore: Surya the Sun gave his son Karna armor and earrings of gold, and Karna was born with them grown into his skin, so that no weapon could kill him. But he had vowed never to refuse a gift, and when the god Indra came in the guise of a begging Brahmin and asked for these as alms, he cut them from his own body and handed them over. So it was that he fell on the seventeenth day at Kurukshetra.

hand_of_glory.name: Hand of Glory
hand_of_glory.lore: Housebreakers in the old tales would cut the hand from a hanged thief, pickle it and dip the fingers in wax to burn as candles, and while it was alight everyone in the house slept and no door stayed locked. Three fingers of this one are yet unburned, and when the last has gone out the hand will fasten upon its bearer and will not let go.

ring_of_protection.name: ring of protection
ring_of_protection.lore: Before he was Archbishop of Canterbury Saint Dunstan was a blacksmith, and they say that when the Devil came to have a hoof shod he nailed on the shoe so painfully that the Devil swore never to enter at any door with iron over it. Rings like this one trade upon that promise: what is aimed at the body of the wearer may land, but the venom, the spell or the fear that it carries will often be turned back at the threshold.

ring_of_solomons_authority.name: Solomon's Authority
ring_of_solomons_authority.unidentified_name: a signet ring with a six-pointed star
ring_of_solomons_authority.lore: From heaven came the ring by which Solomon held command over demons and djinn. With it he enslaved Asmodeus, the king of demons, and forced him to labour upon the building of the Temple, but when a demon stole it Solomon was brought so low that he begged for his food until he recovered it, for the power of the ring depended wholly upon who wore it.

amulet_of_hippolyta.name: Girdle of Hippolyta
amulet_of_hippolyta.lore: Hippolyta, queen of the Amazons, received this war-belt from her father Ares in token that she was first among them. A princess of Mycenae desired it, and so the fetching of it was made the ninth labor of Heracles. Hippolyta came down to his ship ready to yield it freely, but Hera went about in the guise of an Amazon spreading word that the queen was being carried off, and so the meeting ended in battle.

ring_of_regeneration.name: ring of regeneration
ring_of_regeneration.lore: As often as Heracles struck a head from the Hydra of Lerna it grew back double, until his nephew Iolaus seared each stump with a torch. A single drop of that creature's blood went into the cooling of this ring, and what is cut upon its wearer closes and what is broken knits, with a patience that fills surgeons with unease.

amulet_of_constitution.name: amulet of constitution
amulet_of_constitution.lore: Diogenes the Cynic made his home in a storage jar in the marketplace of Athens, and to harden himself he would roll in hot sand in summer and embrace statues covered with snow in winter. He owned almost nothing, though this charm is said to have been among the little that he had, and its wearer shrugs off what would lay others in their beds.

amulet_of_intellect.name: amulet of intellect
amulet_of_intellect.lore: When King Ptolemy inquired whether geometry might not be learned by some shorter way than working through the Elements, Euclid answered that there is no royal road to geometry. Neither will this charm provide one, but whoever wears it travels more quickly along the common road.

amulet_of_wisdom.name: amulet of wisdom
amulet_of_wisdom.lore: Athena had the little owl for her bird, and Athens stamped it upon every coin of silver, so that 'bringing owls to Athens' came to mean the carrying of a thing where there is already plenty. Yet a charm that bears her owl can never be one too many, for the one who wears it sees the consequence before the act.

ring_of_command.name: Ring of Command
ring_of_command.lore: To try Solomon with hard questions the Queen of Sheba journeyed to Jerusalem, and the Book of Kings says that there was none he could not answer for her. His throne had six steps, with a lion at either end of each. This heavy band of gold bears the seal of that throne room, and it will answer only to a judgment that has been weighed and found sufficient.

azaraels_brand.name: Azarael's Brand
azaraels_brand.unidentified_name: a brand on the wrist that is always warm
azaraels_brand.lore: Whoever breaks the chains of a fallen Power is marked by him with a ring of raised bronze skin about the wrist, as warm as a hearthstone. Azarael was one of the Powers before he fell, and he pays his debts in the coin that he has, so that the strength in it is real. But it was never put on as other rings are, and so it can never be taken off, nor will the warmth of it ever fade.

locust_charm.name: Locust Charm
locust_charm.unidentified_name: a dried locust in a cage of black wire
locust_charm.lore: About the neck of everyone who says the words at its checkpoints the Cult of the Locust hangs a dried locust in a little cage of black wire. The charm is no deceit, for while it is worn the swarms of the Destroyer take the wearer for one of their own, and will do that wearer no harm until they are struck. Its price is a single sentence, and the cult intends that sentence to be the first of many.

brass_wardens_cog.name: The Brass Warden's Cog
brass_wardens_cog.unidentified_name: a heavy brass cog on a chain
brass_wardens_cog.lore: The Guild of the Clockwrights paid the best of its counters in cogs cut so true that they never slipped a tooth, and these were worn upon a chain as a mark of the trade. This one came out of the belly of the Brass Warden, still warm from its furnace. If you hold it while you reckon, your count keeps time with its steady tick, and you gain a breath or two before the sum is due. The Guild has been gone these four hundred years, but the cog does not know it, and keeps time as faithfully as ever it did.

black_string_bracelet.name: Black String Bracelet
black_string_bracelet.unidentified_name: a loop of black fiddle string tied round the wrist
black_string_bracelet.lore: Giuseppe Tartini said that the Devil played him a sonata in a dream, and that he spent his life in failing to write it down. With a length of the same string the gentleman at the crossroads binds the wrist of all who sign his paper, and from that hour answers arrive a moment before their questions, which feels every bit as wrong as it sounds. The knot has no ends by which it might be loosed, and payment for it will not fall due until later, much later.

ring_of_wizardry.name: ring of wizardry
ring_of_wizardry.lore: A single hoard at Thebes yielded the books that are called the Greek Magical Papyri, and they are working books, with recipes for summoning, binding and foretelling, and notes in the margins where a spell went amiss. Those who wrote them desired what every worker of magic desires, a spell that costs less than the last, and to that wish this ring was cut.

beeswax_earplugs.name: Beeswax Earplugs
beeswax_earplugs.lore: Odysseus, when he must sail past the Sirens, softened beeswax in the sun and stopped the ears of his crew with it, so that they rowed on deaf while he, bound to the mast, heard the song that kills. These are two plugs of such yellow wax in a twist of cloth. With them in your ears no wail, song or scream can reach your mind, but you will hear nothing else either, neither the horn of a war-band nor the warning growl of a dog.

cold_iron_charm.name: Cold-Iron Charm
cold_iron_charm.unidentified_name: an iron nail on a red thread
cold_iron_charm.lore: Country folk all over Britain and Ireland would nail a horseshoe above the door and lay an iron knife in the cradle, because the Fair Folk cannot abide cold iron. This is a horseshoe nail of that metal, hammered and never heated, hung upon a red thread, and while you carry it their charms, their confusions, their sleeps and their visions will slide away from you.

eyes_of_lamia.name: The Eyes of Lamia
eyes_of_lamia.unidentified_name: a small glass jar with something floating in it
eyes_of_lamia.special: Hera never let her eyes close: whoever wears them cannot be put to sleep or held still.
eyes_of_lamia.lore: Lamia was a queen of Libya whom Zeus loved, and on that account Hera slew her children. Grief made a monster of her, and Hera ordained that she should never close her eyes upon what she had lost, until Zeus in his pity gave her the power to take them out and lay them aside, that she might rest. Plutarch says that she kept them in a jar at home and put them back when she went out hunting. These are the eyes, lying in their jar, and in all the years since her day they have not closed or so much as blinked.

whitethorn_branch.name: Sprig of Whitethorn
whitethorn_branch.unidentified_name: a sprig of white blossom on a thorny twig
whitethorn_branch.lore: When the striges came by night to the cradle of the child Proca, as Ovid tells, the nymph Cranae touched the doorposts three times with arbutus and set a branch of whitethorn in the window, and they never came again. This is a sprig of that same hawthorn of the hedgerows, in white flower, and while it is carried no strix will come at you.

caged_cockerel.name: Caged Cockerel
caged_cockerel.unidentified_name: a red cockerel in a wicker cage
caged_cockerel.lore: A red cockerel sits in this little wicker cage, loud and evil of temper. The old bestiaries teach that the crowing of a cock is death to cockatrice and basilisk, as the weasel is, and in China a rooster's cry sends the hopping dead back to their coffins at dawn. If you let it crow (Apply), every cockatrice or lesser basilisk in earshot will be struck down, and a basilisk or a jiangshi will reel. It will crow but once a floor, and afterward it sulks upon its perch.
